PullRequest.Title: test: keep the real pointer out of Electron unit test windows on Windows and macOS CI
PullRequest.Body:
Fixes a Windows-only PR CI flake in `Artifact Integration Presentation > list rows float their item actions, which run on that item without opening it or closing the panel`. It failed on 6 unrelated PRs in the last 48 hours, always on `Windows / Electron-Unit` and never on Linux or in Browser-Unit:

```
after: [ ..., { label: 'Build', visible: true, trailing: true, centered: true } ]   // expected visible: false
```

## Mechanism

On CI the Electron unit test window is shown with `showInactive()` so Windows doesn't throttle its animation frames. A shown window also receives the real desktop pointer. The item actions in that list are shown for rows matching `:hover`, `:focus-within`, `.focused` or `.selected`. When the runner's cursor rests over the window and Windows delivers mouse moves, which happens as the parallel workers' windows open and close, the second ("Build") row gets `:hover` after the list re-renders, so its actions show even though it isn't focused. Worker windows cascade, so whether the cursor lands on that row varies from run to run.

Linux had the same problem under Xvfb, and #346645 fixed it by moving the pointer off the window after every top-level suite. Windows wasn't covered.

## Change

On CI outside Linux, the test window ignores OS mouse events (`setIgnoreMouseEvents(true)`). Tests drive input through DOM events or `sendInputEvent`, which still reach the page. Linux keeps the existing per-suite pointer reset.

## Validation

Local repro on Windows, with the CI window mode (`GITHUB_WORKSPACE` set), the test window kept on top as on a runner, and the cursor moving over the Build row:
- `main`: failed 2 of 3 runs, with the exact CI diff above. With the cursor elsewhere on the same window it passes.
- this change: 9 of 9 runs pass.
- Broader CI-mode run with this change (`vs/base/test/browser`, sessions and webview browser tests): 10,520 passing, 0 failing.

> Authored with Copilot

Scenarios.Scenario: Windows/macOS CI Electron unit-test worker startup and normal test execution
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Each worker creates a BrowserWindow, synchronously calls setIgnoreMouseEvents(true), then starts loading renderer.html; the added native call must return before loadURL is issued, but it is one constant-time call per window rather than work repeated per test, suite, frame, or input event.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create the Electron renderer process associated with each BrowserWindow.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One renderer per worker or serialized rerun window; parallel cardinality is bounded by the pre-existing worker count.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same BrowserWindow and renderer process were created for every worker and rerun.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Renderer creation and readiness are on test startup's critical path, but the diff does not add or increase renderer creation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Tell Electron/the native window system to ignore real OS mouse events for the test window.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Exactly once per Windows/macOS CI test window.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No native ignore-mouse-events setting was applied; the shown CI window continued receiving real pointer events.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: This synchronous native call occurs before loadURL, but has constant cardinality and no realistic scaling mechanism relative to the already-required window creation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Load the local renderer.html page and its test runner modules into the renderer.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Once per test window, followed by the existing module loads selected for that worker.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same local page and modules were loaded after window creation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Page/module loading remains on startup's critical path; the diff neither adds loads nor changes their cardinality.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Spawn bounded parallel Electron unit-test worker processes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: The existing configured worker count, with one test window per child process.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same number of worker processes were spawned concurrently.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Workers execute concurrently and each performs the added constant-time native call once; the diff does not create workers or increase concurrency.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: The number of Electron worker windows: normally one per worker process, plus one replacement window for each configured failed-test rerun in a non-worker process. It does not scale with the number of loaded tests or pointer events.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: A worker process has one live test window for the first attempt; reruns are serialized and the prior window is destroyed. Parallel first attempts use the existing bounded worker count, so at most one added call executes in each worker process concurrently.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache is involved. Cold and warm starts both make exactly one setIgnoreMouseEvents call for each newly created window; there are no keys, misses, retries, or coalescing concerns.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence: the condition, call count, ordering before loadURL, serialized reruns, and bounded parallel-worker topology are explicit in the traced code.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The exact native-call duration varies by OS/Electron implementation, but it is a single call per heavyweight window startup and has no repeated or collection-scaling path.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The only added work is one constant-time native window configuration call per Windows/macOS CI window, while all heavyweight renderer, filesystem, and worker-process boundaries retain their previous cardinality and concurrency.

Scenarios.Scenario: Linux CI Electron unit-test suites and per-suite hover reset
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The new platform guard skips setIgnoreMouseEvents entirely on Linux. Existing top-level suite cleanup invokes an IPC handler that sends a synthetic mouseLeave; that path is unchanged by the diff.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Invoke vscode:test-pointer-leave from the renderer and send a mouseLeave input event from the main process after each top-level suite.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One existing IPC round trip per top-level suite per Linux worker.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Linux already used the same per-suite IPC reset before this diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Suite isolation waits for the reset, but this boundary is unchanged and the added branch does not execute on Linux.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Top-level suite count controls the existing Linux mouseLeave IPC frequency, but effective changed-code cardinality is zero on Linux.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Each renderer performs its suite resets in its own bounded worker process; the diff adds no Linux work or concurrency.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache is involved. The platform branch deterministically bypasses the new call on every Linux window.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the explicit process.platform !== 'linux' guard and the unchanged Linux reset implementation.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: None material for PR causality: the changed native call is unreachable on Linux.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance change on Linux; the pre-existing per-suite IPC remains unchanged.

Scenarios.Scenario: Local Electron unit tests and developer-mode windows
Scenarios.CriticalPath: When CI environment variables are absent, execution bypasses the entire showInactive/setIgnoreMouseEvents block and proceeds to renderer loading as before.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create renderer and optional worker processes for local Electron tests.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical local renderer and worker creation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: These existing boundaries remain on startup's critical path, but no changed operation runs locally.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Any number of local runs or selected test files has zero added call cardinality because isCI is false.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Existing local worker and rerun behavior is unchanged; the added call never executes.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache is involved; the environment predicate deterministically excludes this path.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the explicit isCI guard.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: None material because the changed branch is unreachable outside CI.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed the sole changed hunk and traced CI/non-CI platform branches, window lifecycle, reruns, parallel worker creation, renderer loading, and Linux suite-reset IPC. The PR adds one constant-time native call per Windows/macOS CI BrowserWindow and does not increase expensive boundary cardinality, retention, or concurrency. No valid performance finding or regression-fix learning signal was identified.
